known.title: Request correction 2 narrows the user's explicit full-gate request to the plan-lifecycle selected gate on the false premise that the shared release engine is plan-lifecycle's descriptor-owned tooling, so the required full gate never runs.
known.locator: Research, Request corrections, Request correction 2 (line 56); Steps row 9 verify_local (line 74); Acceptance a15 (line 94)
known.summary: Request correction 2 replaces the asked-for full `node scripts/ci.mjs` with `node scripts/ci.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle`, and verify_local and a15 carry it out. Its premise is false at repo_ref: `scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs` is the one generic release engine for all three plugins (`scripts/release.mjs:4-6` 'Generic positional lane (Docks, Effect Kit, and Plan Lifecycle)', `scripts/AGENTS.md:29`, `:187`), and no descriptor owns it (`releaseContracts: []` for docks, effect-kit, and plan-lifecycle at `scripts/lib/plugins.mjs:67`, `:86`, `:112`). `AGENTS.md:143` and `scripts/AGENTS.md:6` route 'shared infrastructure used by multiple plugins' and 'manual full-gate requests' to the full gate, and the user made exactly such a request. The effect is real, not only a rule breach: with `--plugin`, `repoWide` is false (`scripts/ci.mjs:222`), so the whole `if (repoWide)` block at `scripts/ci.mjs:260-319` is skipped, including `scripts/ci.mjs:306-307` (`ci-plugin-targeting.mjs --unit`, the suite this plan changes) and `scripts/ci.mjs:290` (durable-anchors over the edited `scripts/AGENTS.md`). Biome then checks only plan-lifecycle's paths (`scripts/lib/plugins.mjs:97-100` unioned at `scripts/ci.mjs:240-250`); `scripts` belongs to docks (`scripts/lib/plugins.mjs:57`), so `scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs` and `scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs` are neither formatted nor linted. Scenario: a15 exits 0 while a Biome or durable-anchor failure in the changed files stays undetected, and the user's explicit request is not met. Fix: drop the correction, run full `node scripts/ci.mjs` in verify_local, and make a15 the full gate.

known.title: Research claims that testGenericReleaseModuleContract runs on every suite invocation, but its only caller is the flag-gated --dry-run-release-safety scenario, so the new release assertions never run in the default or --unit mode, in the gate, or in CI.
known.locator: Research, Repository facts, 'The test home' (line 30); Steps row 6 contract_tests (line 71); Acceptance a2 to a10 (lines 81-89)
known.summary: Line 30 states that `testGenericReleaseModuleContract` (`scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs:848-1099`) runs in the default mode (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:208-211`) and the `--unit` mode (`scripts/ci.mjs:307`). At repo_ref its only call is `scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs:1126`, inside `testDryRunReleaseSafety` (`:1101-1256`), whose only call is `:1315` under `if (mode === '--dry-run-release-safety')` (`:1314-1318`). The default and `--unit` paths continue at `:1324` and never call it, and nothing in `scripts/ci.mjs` or any workflow passes that flag. contract_tests puts every new assertion in that function and no step moves its call onto the default path. Scenario: a2 to a7 expect `node scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs` to run the new assertions, but it exits 0 without running them; a8 to a10 expect exit 1 after a production revert, but the default suite still exits 0; the gate and CI never exercise the re-cut preview. Fix: correct the claim and add a step that calls the contract from the suite's default path outside `if (!unitOnly)` (so both the default and `--unit` modes run it), with an Acceptance row that the contract runs in both modes.

protected.summary: User: keep the executed `createGenericPluginReleaseIo.commit` unchanged (same `git add`, same `git diff --cached --quiet -- <files>` test, same early return, sentence bytes only moved behind a shared constant) and give the preview its own read-only staging probe instead of moving the commit decision into the engine. Sound: the premise holds at repo_ref; `scripts/AGENTS.md:187` preserves the positional flow's existing 'commit/push/tag behavior', and the re-cut branch at `scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:395-405` is the recovery that `:343-350` prints. The two predicates cannot disagree on the path where the preview predicts: on a clean tree `git status --porcelain` is empty, so the index equals HEAD, and `git add` stages a change exactly when the filtered blob differs from `HEAD:<path>`, which `git hash-object --path <path> --stdin` computes without `-w` (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-hash-object, https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff). On a dirty tree the release refuses at `:271`, and clean_gate reports that. Keeping a released, working path is not a workaround or an obsolete path under the snapshot contract's durable-fix rule or `AGENTS.md`, and a11 checks it.

User: report a noncanonical manifest (formatting-only label plus a predicted commit) instead of forbidding it; add no canonical-bytes gate check and reformat no manifest. Sound: at repo_ref all seven files that the release writes (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and both `plugin.json` files of docks, effect-kit, and plan-lifecycle) are byte-equal to `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` plus a newline (checked by parse and re-serialize), `io.writeJson` at `scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:524-526` restores canonical bytes on every release write, and the staging probe makes the preview true for any byte form, so no Goal outcome depends on enforcement. No existing gate check enforces canonical bytes (`javascriptQuality` paths at `scripts/lib/plugins.mjs:56-59`, `:78`, `:97-100` and `check:js` at `package.json:12` cover no manifest; no byte check in `scripts/ci.mjs`), so nothing is left on a replaced path. The root cause (the preview's blind predicate) is fixed by preview_truth, which meets the snapshot contract's durable-fix rule; no instruction file at repo_ref requires canonical-bytes enforcement.

Request correction: the user asked that the preview say 'unchanged' and 'tags the existing HEAD' whenever the manifests already carry the version; the plan says so only when `git add` of the written bytes would stage nothing, and gives a same-version manifest with other bytes the formatting-only label and a predicted commit. Sound: `io.writeJson` at `scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:524-526` always writes `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` plus a newline, and `commit` at `scripts/lib/plugin-release.mjs:400` branches on `git diff --cached --quiet`, which exits 0 only when nothing is staged relative to HEAD (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff). A version-equality test would print 'unchanged' for a noncanonical manifest that the release rewrites, stages, and commits, which contradicts the Goal's 'never promises a commit that the release skips or hides one that the release makes'. preview_truth and predict_commit carry it out, and a2/a3/a13 check both branches; it breaks no rule of `AGENTS.md`, `scripts/AGENTS.md`, or the v3 contract.
